facts.raw_span: A 30-year-old man with no prior medical or psychiatric history
sudden onset of painless bilateral loss of vision
immediately after falling approximately 3 meters from a pickup truck
resulting in a concussion and a superficial scalp laceration
Glasgow Coma Scale score 15
visual acuity of counting fingers bilaterally
no light perception in both eyes
Systemic and neurologic examinations were otherwise unremarkable
Noncontrast computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging of the brain showed no abnormalities
Visual evoked potentials were normal
electroretinography indicated no pathologic process
referred for psychiatric evaluation to rule out conversion disorder
